question: Between 1994 and 2014, 1 500 girls in the UK were victims of sexual violence, often rape, at the hands of a huge organised gang of Pakistani-origin men, something now sadly known as a ‘grooming gang’. At the time, Keir Starmer, who is now the Prime Minister and Labour Party leader, was the head of the Crown Prosecution Service, which was in charge of the case.

These events resurfaced as a result of posts by billionaire and X owner Elon Musk. They have provoked global outrage and given rise to questions about the roles played by both Keir Starmer (who was responsible for handling the case) and the British Government in dealing with and potentially even covering up these crimes.
On 9 January 2025, Labour voted in the UK Parliament to reject the call for a parliamentary inquiry. 1.
What is the Council’s position on this matter?
Does it condemn the abuse committed?
Should the allegations about the role played by politicians be substantiated, what measures can the Council adopt?
answer: EN Reply (19.5.2025) It is not for the Council to comment on posts on social media or articles appearing in the press. Moreover, the matter referred to does not fall within the jurisdiction of the Union.
